guard.reason: threshold breached 2 samples in a row: recommendation p95_ms (10620.5ms > 104.6ms); frontend p95_ms (8253.9ms > 133.6ms); product-catalog p95_ms (7142.2ms > 119.6ms); frontend-proxy p95_ms (6307.1ms > 132.7ms)

limitations: Stopped after 9s, so the evidence covers only the start of the fault

verdict.explanation: The experiment successfully demonstrated that injecting 200ms of network delay into astronomy-db significantly increased p95 latency across dependent services on the checkout path (frontend, frontend-proxy, product-catalog, and recommendation) while error rates remained essentially at zero (with a tiny 1.27% increase on frontend-proxy), fully supporting the hypothesis.

claims.claim: adding network delay to astronomy-db will increase p95 latency for services querying the database on the checkout path
claims.evidence: recommendation p95_ms increased from 4.58 to 10620.46ms, product-catalog p95_ms increased from 19.62 to 7142.18ms, frontend p95_ms increased from 33.63 to 8253.95ms, and frontend-proxy p95_ms increased from 32.69 to 6307.13ms.

claims.claim: adding network delay to astronomy-db will not cause widespread uncaught errors
claims.evidence: error rates remained at 0.0 for frontend, product-catalog, and recommendation, with a minimal increase to 1.27 for frontend-proxy.

verdict.recommendation: Implement bounded timeouts and circuit breakers on the product-catalog and recommendation services when querying astronomy-db to prevent severe latency amplification and thread pool exhaustion.
